what_is_real: All UI is the real RecipeFix web app at e68b1404 rendered by Chrome; no DOM injected, restyled or mocked.

Every interaction is a real Playwright touch tap on the real control: landing composer (paste link, Dairy-Free, + servings x2, Adapt recipe), the coconut-yogurt ingredient row, Cook, Start cooking, Next, Start 20:00 timer.
The adaptation payload is the stored production adapt-recipe response in src/data/landingRealResult.ts (served by the harness for exactly this request).
The Cook Mode timer is the app's own countdown running in real time.
what_is_simulated: Backend: every *.supabase.co request is answered in-process by tooling/journey-capture.mjs (= scripts/journey.mjs @ e68b1404, only import paths/ROOT changed; see journey-capture.diff). Nothing reached Supabase, OpenAI, recipefix.app or any production host.
Stream timing: the working card's SSE events are re-paced by the harness (~5 s). The 'Usually about 20 seconds' copy is production's; the on-screen duration is not real latency.

Hero photo: the result arrives without a photo, the client calls preview-recipe (answered by the harness), so a pulsing skeleton shows ~0.9 s before the photo fades in. Real behaviour, harness timing.
estimate-nutrition is aborted by the harness (panel shows the payload's own estimate). rescale-recipe/refine-recipe return 503.
Scrolls are scripted (eased cubic). Scroll segments are FRAME-STEPPED (see video_method); holds/taps/transitions are real-time.

viewport.browser: system Google Chrome via playwright-core (from the worktree node_modules)

video_method.encode: ffmpeg -framerate 60 -i o%05d.png -vf format=yuv420p -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 12 -profile:v high -movflags +faststart (H.264 High, 1170x2532, yuv420p, 60 fps CFR)
video_method.realtime_segments: CDP Page.startScreencast PNG frames at 1170x2532 (Chromium compositor output), each held until the next frame, sampled at exactly 1/60 s.
video_method.stepped_segments: Scrolls. Measured: the page itself scrolls at a clean 60 fps (134 rAFs over 2.2 s, no gap > 25 ms) but screencast at this size dropped 50-133 ms of frames mid-scroll (judder). So each scroll is rendered as ms*60/1000 positions on the same easing curve: set scroll position, wait two rAFs, CDP Page.captureScreenshot (device px), one output frame each. The clip therefore shows the true page at each position; only wall-clock pacing of the scroll is synthetic.
video_method.assembly: tooling/assemble.py (cuts by logged marks; timelines in tooling/run-logs/timeline-*.json)

recipefix-v2-clip3-servings.why: Not recorded per brief. The stepper is client-side first (applyClientServingsScale rewrites amounts instantly, verified 6->7: '1⅛ cups plus 2 tablespoons … coconut yogurt', '3½ tablespoons vegan butter', '⅞ cup … coconut cream') but 1.5 s later handleServingsChange calls rescale-recipe, which the harness refuses with 503; the client keeps its own math, logs 'rescale-recipe failed, keeping frontend scale' and shows a 'Scaled to 7 servings · View' toast. In production the AI rescale would replace those lines, so the recorded result would not be what a user sees. Probe screenshots: tooling/run-logs/servings-*.png.

network.summary: No request reached production. *.supabase.co requests were fulfilled or aborted in-process by Playwright routes (never sent); a final catch-all route aborted anything else non-local; and Chrome's host resolver mapped supabase/openai/recipefix/posthog/googleapis/lovable to 0.0.0.0 as a second barrier. Only Google Fonts and 127.0.0.1 were allowed out.

The 503 is the servings probe's rescale-recipe. No page errors.
